events.text: Chris Haney and Scott Abbott devise Trivial Pursuit in Montreal
Ernő Rubik invents his twisting cube puzzle in Budapest
Arthur Wynne's word-cross, the first crossword puzzle, runs in a New York paper

reveal.explanation: The word-cross puzzle that grew into the crossword appeared in a newspaper in 1913, and Parker Brothers took Monopoly to market in 1935. Ernő Rubik's cube arrived in 1974 and was still a craze when two Canadian journalists devised Trivial Pursuit in 1979.

sources.excerpt: On December 21, 1913, Arthur Wynne, a journalist born in Liverpool, England, published a "word-cross" puzzle in the New York World that embodied most of the features of the modern genre.
Parker Brothers first published Monopoly in 1935.
The Rubik's Cube is a 3D combination puzzle invented in 1974 by Hungarian sculptor and professor of architecture Ernő Rubik.
The game was created on December 15, 1979, in Montreal, Quebec, by Canadians Chris Haney, a photo editor for Montreal's The Gazette, and Scott Abbott, a sports editor for The Canadian Press.
